questions.stem: The suffix '-able' (as in readable, achievable, comfortable) typically indicates:

options.option_text: Capable of being / fit for / suitable for the action

questions.explanation: -ABLE / -IBLE — adjective-forming suffix meaning 'capable of being [verb]ed'. Readable = capable of being read. Achievable = able to be achieved. Audible = capable of being heard. Visible = capable of being seen. Convertible = able to be converted. -able usually attaches to verbs of native English origin; -ible attaches to Latin-origin verbs (visible, edible, terrible). The two are interchangeable in some words; spelling must be memorised.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Which suffix is added to verbs to form a noun for the PERFORMER of the action (e.g., teacher, runner, actor)?
questions.explanation: -ER / -OR — agent suffix from verb → noun (the doer). teach → teacher, run → runner, act → actor, edit → editor, paint → painter. Generally -er for English-origin and -or for Latin-origin (though not always). Compare other agent-formers: -ist (artist, scientist), -ant/-ent (assistant, student), -ian (musician), -ive (executive). Confusion trap: in 'runner', the consonant doubles before -er (one-syllable verbs ending in single consonant after single vowel double the consonant).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The suffix '-ity' typically converts an adjective into:

options.option_text: An abstract noun denoting the QUALITY or STATE

questions.explanation: -ITY — Latin-origin abstract-noun suffix. Pure → purity (state of being pure). Active → activity (state of being active). Equal → equality. Real → reality. Brief → brevity (irregular). Compare other quality-noun formers: -NESS (kindness, happiness, darkness — Germanic origin); -SHIP (friendship, leadership); -HOOD (childhood, neighbourhood); -DOM (freedom, kingdom).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Which of these words is correctly formed with a suffix?
questions.explanation: -LY — adverb-forming suffix from adjective: beautiful → beautifully, quick → quickly, careful → carefully. Spelling rule: when the adjective ends in '-y' preceded by consonant, change y to i + add -ly: happy → happily, easy → easily. When ending in '-le', drop e + add y: gentle → gently, simple → simply. -LY also forms adjectives from nouns: friend → friendly, day → daily — easy trap.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The suffix '-ous' (as in famous, dangerous, courageous) creates:

options.option_text: Adjectives meaning 'full of / possessing the quality of'

questions.explanation: -OUS — Latin-origin adjective suffix from noun. Fame → famous (full of fame). Danger → dangerous. Courage → courageous. Joy → joyous. Note spelling shifts: glory → glorious; victory → victorious. Compare similar adjective-formers: -FUL (helpful, beautiful — full of); -LESS (helpless, hopeless — without); -LIKE (childlike, lifelike — resembling); -ISH (childish, foolish — having qualities of); -Y (rainy, windy, lucky — characterised by).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Match suffix to its meaning — which pair is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: -CRACY (Greek 'kratos') = power / rule, NOT wealth. Democracy (rule by the people), autocracy (rule by one), aristocracy (rule by elite), bureaucracy (rule by office), theocracy (rule by religion), plutocracy (rule by the wealthy — note 'pluto-' is wealth, not 'cracy'). Other meaningful suffixes: -PHOBIA (fear: claustrophobia, hydrophobia); -CIDE (killer / killing: pesticide, suicide, homicide); -OLOGY (study of: biology, geology, sociology); -PHILE (lover of: bibliophile); -GAMY (marriage: monogamy, polygamy).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The suffix '-tion' / '-sion' forms what part of speech?
questions.explanation: -TION / -SION — Latin abstract-noun suffix from verb. Educate → education. Decide → decision. Communicate → communication. Translate → translation. Convert → conversion. Permit → permission. Choose between -tion / -sion is mostly orthographic — verbs ending in -t / -te take -tion; verbs ending in -d / -de or -mit / -ss take -sion. Other verb→noun suffixes: -MENT (judgement, payment, agreement), -ANCE / -ENCE (assistance, performance, existence), -AL (refusal, arrival), -URE (failure, departure).
